aboutH2: Sobriety.ca Foundation: a small residential rehab between Ottawa and Montreal
intro: Sobriety.ca Foundation is a not-for-profit that runs a live-in addiction treatment centre called Sobriety Home. Its admissions office is on the 11th floor of 343 Preston Street in Ottawa, but treatment does not happen there. The residence is a converted farm property on Route 138 in Godmanchester, Quebec, near Huntingdon in the Haut-Saint-Laurent. The centre puts the drive from Ottawa at under two hours, and Montreal is about an hour away.

The house takes no more than 12 clients at a time, all adults 18 and over, and each one gets a private room with a private bathroom. People come for alcohol, drugs, prescription medication and gambling. You can refer yourself without a doctor's letter, and the centre also accepts pets, which is rare for a residential program.

pillars.title: An Old Farm Property in the Haut-Saint-Laurent
pillars.body: Sobriety Home sits on more than two acres of farmland along Route 138 in Godmanchester, a rural township near Huntingdon in southwestern Quebec. Several buildings are spread across the property, including stone-walled group rooms, barns turned into common spaces, a gym and a separate house where the women sleep. In summer people use the pool and the patios. The New York border is about ten minutes south, Montreal is about an hour away, and the centre puts Ottawa at under two hours, close enough for family visits.

pillars.title: Online Aftercare and an Exit Plan
pillars.body: Before you go home you work out a written exit plan with your counsellor. Graduates then get access to the centre's online aftercare platform, where trained facilitators run group meetings that you join from a computer or phone. The centre says it stays in touch with clients and their families for more than a year, and family and spousal counselling carry on as part of that extended aftercare. People who left treatment early can arrange a shorter stay only if it comes with more aftercare and outpatient counselling.

pillars.title: A Nurse, a Weekly Doctor and Master's-Level Therapists
pillars.body: A registered nurse works on site, a local physician sees each resident once a week, and a consulting psychiatrist is available for concurrent mental health conditions. The centre says all of its therapists and counsellors hold a master's degree or higher. A trained fitness counsellor runs the gym program, and Native elders lead healing circles and sweat lodge ceremonies. Staff can collect you anywhere within 100 kilometres of the house, or from the airport or train station.

overview: Care runs in three stages. New arrivals who need it go through medical detox on site, which averages about seven days. A short rest period of up to 48 hours follows for anyone who is stable but worn out, and then the core treatment program begins. That program usually lasts at least 30 days and can run longer. A registered nurse works on site, a local physician sees every resident once a week, and a consulting psychiatrist handles concurrent conditions such as depression, anxiety and PTSD. The physician can prescribe anti-craving medication, including methadone and Suboxone.
serviceCaption: 11 services · as described on the centre's website
afterOverview: Individual therapy is required for everyone. Group sessions are suggested case by case, and family and spousal counselling are offered as well. The centre describes its approach as non-12-step and medical-psychological, built on CBT, DBT, psychodynamic and trauma therapy, with SMART Recovery and an introduction to the 12 steps for those who want it. Yoga, massage, art therapy and an on-site gym fill out the days. Women sleep in a separate house from the men and have women-only sessions, while most groups are mixed.

location.heading: Sobriety.ca Foundation in Godmanchester, Quebec
location.intro: Treatment happens at the residence on Route 138 in Godmanchester, a farming township near Huntingdon in the Haut-Saint-Laurent part of Montérégie. Downtown Montreal is about an hour and ten minutes away by car, Salaberry-de-Valleyfield about half an hour, and the centre puts Ottawa at under two hours; admissions calls go through the foundation's office at 343 Preston Street in Ottawa.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's own website and public listings. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Where does treatment at Sobriety.ca Foundation actually take place?
faqs.a: Treatment takes place at Sobriety Home, a residential centre on Route 138 in Godmanchester, Quebec, near Huntingdon. The 11th floor office at 343 Preston Street in Ottawa is the foundation's admissions office, not a treatment site. The residence is under two hours from Ottawa by car and about an hour from Montreal.

faqs.q: Is Sobriety.ca Foundation residential or outpatient?
faqs.a: It is a residential program: you live at the Godmanchester house for the length of your stay. Detox happens on site, and aftercare after discharge is online. The centre's recent articles also mention online therapy and outpatient options, so ask admissions what is available if you cannot leave home.

faqs.q: Is Sobriety.ca Foundation connected to Heritage Home Foundation?
faqs.a: Yes, they share one residence. Both official websites give 2678 Route 138 in Godmanchester as the treatment facility, and sobriety.ca itself describes Heritage Home Foundation as the non-profit residential centre in Godmanchester. Heritage takes Montreal enquiries through an office at 1200 McGill College Avenue and calls the residence one of the few English-speaking rehabs in Quebec. Sobriety.ca handles admissions from its Ottawa office.

faqs.q: Is the Sobriety.ca Foundation residence licensed by Quebec?
faqs.a: Yes. The Quebec Ministry of Health and Social Services (MSSS) directory of addiction resources lists the residence at 2678 Route 138 in Godmanchester under the name Heritage Home Foundation inc., the name the same house uses for its Montreal marketing. It is on the list of Montérégie residences that hold an authorization to offer addiction treatment with lodging, now issued by Santé Québec in place of the older CISSS certification. The entry, last updated October 7, 2026, lists room for 12 adults, withdrawal support of 7 to 10 days and therapy of 30 to 90 days. You can check it at msss.gouv.qc.ca/repertoires/dependances/fiche_public.php?nofiche=246.

faqs.q: Is Sobriety.ca Foundation the same as Sobriety House in Ottawa?
faqs.a: No. Sobriety House is a separate men's recovery home at 90 First Avenue in Ottawa. Sobriety.ca Foundation is a different not-for-profit whose treatment centre, Sobriety Home, is in rural Quebec. The two have similar names but are not connected.

Yes. Medical detox is done at the residence and lasts about seven days on average, under the direction of the centre's affiliated physician with staff on site around the clock. A registered nurse works at the house and a physician visits weekly, so withdrawal can be handled before the main program starts.

The core treatment program is usually at least 30 days. The centre says the length depends on your needs and on availability, and stays can run longer, up to three months. Shorter stays are only arranged with the Clinical Director when they come with more intensive aftercare.

faqs.q: How much does Sobriety.ca Foundation cost?
faqs.a: The centre does not publish its prices. Its admissions page asks you to contact the team directly about rates and payment. It is a private-pay program, and it accepts major credit cards, personal cheques and bank drafts.

Adults 18 and older with an alcohol, drug or gambling problem can apply, as long as they are able to take part in the whole program. Self-referrals are welcome, so you do not need a referral from a doctor. You start by filling in the online admission application, and someone from the centre calls you back.
Yes. The centre says pets are welcome and that they help residents feel calmer and more supported. Mention your pet when you first call so the team can plan for it.

faqs.q: How do I get to the residence?
faqs.a: You can drive in, or staff can pick you up anywhere within 100 kilometres of the centre. They also collect people from airports and train stations. For flights inside Canada the centre suggests Montreal-Trudeau Airport; from the US, Burlington and Plattsburgh airports and nearby Amtrak stations are options. The house is about ten minutes from the New York state border.

faqs.q: Is there a program for women?
faqs.a: Yes. Women sleep in a separate house away from the men's quarters and have access to women-only group sessions. Most therapy groups are mixed, which the centre says helps people prepare for life back home. Counsellors are trained to work with trauma, including sexual and physical violence.

You leave with a written exit plan and access to the centre's online aftercare platform. Graduates join group meetings by computer or phone, run by trained facilitators. The centre says it stays in contact with clients and their families for over a year, with family counselling available as part of extended aftercare.
